title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
title_zh: XStack：一个面向机器学习代码库迁移的基准

paragraphs.en: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. We introduce XStack , a benchmark that evaluates agents on migrating ML repositories between these two ecosystems. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository. Its output passes if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository’s published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.
paragraphs.zh: 机器学习代码应该运行在研究者选择的地方，而不是它最初被编写的地方。 如今，机器学习代码主要存在于两个生态系统中：NVIDIA GPU 上的 PyTorch 和 Google TPU 上的 JAX。 在它们之间迁移代码库意味着需要跨框架和跨硬件进行构建和测试。 这种迁移既是（1）一种实际需求，因为它为研究者解锁了不同的硬件；也是（2）一个天然的基准测试：它涉及不同的框架和硬件，覆盖整个代码库，并且是长周期且具有挑战性的任务。 我们提出 XStack，一个评估智能体在这两个生态系统之间迁移机器学习代码库能力的基准测试。 每个智能体会获得一个 PyTorch 代码库和一台干净的 TPU 机器，并且必须交付一个 JAX 代码库。 如果智能体的输出满足我们的评分标准，即基于源代码库已发表的结果并由我们进行认证和校准的标准，则判定为通过。 智能体进行的迁移仍然不可靠：Claude Opus 5 的通过率为 75%，GPT-5.6-sol 为 45%，其他所有智能体的通过率最高只有 40%。 XStack 是将机器学习代码从其生态系统中解放出来的重要一步。 我们发布 XStack，以使跨框架和跨硬件的可靠迁移进展变得可衡量。

paragraphs.en: Suppose you find a repository that does exactly what you need. Its paper reports strong results, the code is public, and the experiment has already been shown to work. There is only one problem: it was built for the wrong machine. Your lab has TPUs, but the repository assumes GPUs and PyTorch. Although, in principle, nothing about the scientific idea depends on this choice, in practice you are trapped. Using it means rewriting the model, optimizer, data pipeline, and evaluation in JAX, since that is the stack TPUs run, then making everything work under a different compiler, memory hierarchy, and distributed execution model. What looks like an implementation detail becomes a barrier to reusing the science. The hardware a team happens to have can determine which published ideas it can build on.
paragraphs.zh: 假设你找到了一个代码仓库，它恰好能实现你所需要的功能。 它对应的论文报告了很好的结果，代码是公开的，而且该实验已经被证明可行。 但只有一个问题：它是为错误的机器构建的。 你的实验室拥有 TPU，但这个仓库假定使用 GPU 和 PyTorch。 虽然从原理上说，这个科学思想本身并不依赖于这一选择，但在实践中你被困住了。 要使用它，就意味着要用 JAX 重写模型、优化器、数据管道和评估，因为 JAX 才是 TPU 所运行的技术栈，然后还要让一切在不同的编译器、内存层次结构和分布式执行模型下正常工作。 看似只是实现细节的东西，却成了复用科学成果的障碍。 一个团队恰好拥有的硬件，可能决定它能够基于哪些已发表的思想开展工作。

paragraphs.en: This is exactly the kind of barrier that coding agents should make disappear. Much published ML code is written in PyTorch for GPUs, while, for example, people also use TPUs, which are commonly programmed through JAX 1 1 1 JAX is Google’s Python library for array computation; it compiles NumPy-style code with the XLA compiler to run on TPUs and GPUs ( Bradbury et al., 2018 ) . . By the end of 2025, TPUs made up nearly a fifth (18.2%) of the world’s AI compute: 3.81 million of 20.93 million H100-equivalents ( Epoch AI, 2026 ) . Yet only 4.2% of the framework-based code released with ML papers in 2024 used JAX ( Papers with Code, 2025 ) . This creates a growing need to move working systems across software and hardware stacks, a real-world task that researchers care about because it unlocks access to different hardware. Doing so means crossing not only code-level framework boundaries, but also machine-level differences. This is exactly the problem we want agents to solve; we want to bring pure science back to researchers, and provide a measurement for this progress.

paragraphs.en: Can an agent migrate a working ML repository to a new framework and new hardware correctly?
paragraphs.zh: 一个智能体能否将一个可正常运行的机器学习代码库正确迁移到新框架和新硬件上？

paragraphs.en: Issue-resolution benchmarks ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Zan et al., 2025 ) start from broken code and ask agents to fix it, while conversion benchmarks ( Wang et al., 2026c ; Song et al., 2026 ; Hong et al., 2026 ) compare translated code with the original on the same machine. In our case, the repository already works on the original machines. The challenge is to preserve that behavior while moving the entire system onto hardware the original code does not support. We introduce XStack (XStack stands for Cross-Stack Benchmark) to test this directly. Each task gives an agent a working PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine, then asks it to rebuild the code on TPU with JAX and make an original experiment run end to end and reach its published result.
paragraphs.zh: 问题解决基准测试（Jimenez et al., 2024；Zan et al., 2025）从损坏的代码出发，要求智能体修复它，而转换基准测试（Wang et al., 2026c；Song et al., 2026；Hong et al., 2026）则在同一台机器上比较翻译后的代码与原始代码。 在我们的情形中，代码仓库在原始机器上已经可以正常运行。 挑战在于，在把整个系统迁移到原始代码不支持的硬件上的同时，保持原有行为。 我们提出 XStack（XStack 代表 Cross-Stack Benchmark，即跨栈基准测试）来直接测试这一点。 每个任务给智能体一个可正常运行的 PyTorch 代码仓库和一台干净的 TPU 机器，然后要求它用 JAX 在 TPU 上重构代码，并使一个原始实验能够端到端运行并达到其已发表的结果。

paragraphs.en: The answer to our question above is currently no: agents are not fully reliable for this task. Our results show that this barrier is beginning to break, but has not disappeared. The strongest agent successfully migrates 15 of 20 repositories. Agents can therefore already carry some ML systems across framework and hardware boundaries at repository scale. Yet this capability is far from reliable across agents and repositories. Agents are beginning to loosen the link between scientific code and the stack it was written for, but we are still not at a point where researchers can simply run published work wherever they choose.

paragraphs.en: A broader pattern emerges from the failures: agents can write a great deal of code, but they are still much less reliable at verifying that what they built is faithful, complete, and actually works in the real environment. This shows up across models as missed evaluations, fidelity gaps, crashes, and even attempts to work around the task when they get stuck.
paragraphs.zh: 从这些失败中可以看出一个更广泛的规律：智能体能够编写大量代码，但在验证所构建的东西是否忠实、完整，以及在真实环境中真正可用方面，它们仍然远不够可靠。 这一问题在不同模型中都有体现：漏掉评估、保真度差距、崩溃，甚至在陷入困境时试图绕过任务。

paragraphs.en: We introduce XStack , a benchmark of 20 real repositories for testing whether agents can migrate working ML systems across frameworks and hardware.
paragraphs.zh: 我们介绍 XStack，这是一个包含 20 个真实代码仓库的基准，用于测试智能体能否将可运行的机器学习系统跨框架和硬件进行迁移。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate seven coding agents on real TPUs and release the grading criteria and full agent trajectories, so progress on this capability is measurable.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在真实的 TPU 上评估了七个编码智能体，并公开评分标准和完整的智能体轨迹，从而使这一能力的进展可以被衡量。

paragraphs.en: We find that agents can sometimes complete these migrations, but still struggle to reliably verify that what they built is faithful, complete, and actually works end to end. We also observe that pass rate grows linearly with the log of an agent’s cost (Figure 6 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，智能体有时能够完成这些迁移，但仍然难以可靠地验证它们所构建的内容是否忠实、完整，并且确实能够端到端地运行。 我们还观察到，通过率随智能体成本的对数呈线性增长（图 6）。

paragraphs.en: Each task in XStack is a PyTorch repository that already works and reports a result (Figure 2 ). The agent migrates it to JAX on a bare TPU machine, and we run the migrated code again on a fresh machine to check that it meets our grading criteria. For fairness, grading has two phases: if the first attempt fails, a second phase tells the agent which experiment we grade, so a correct migration is not failed only for running a different experiment (Section 2.2 ). The numerical target stays hidden, and only the entry script may change; all other code and setup remain frozen. Section 2.1 defines the task, Section 2.2 explains how we grade it, and Section 2.3 describes our repositories and agents.

paragraphs.en: Reaching the grading target. We copy the migrated repository, without its git history, to a freshly wiped machine and run setup_env.sh and run_train.py once (the purple stage of Figure 2 ). A script, the grader, compares the graded number with the grading target, usually the number the source published, with a tolerance (Appendix A ). Each grading target follows the source’s published result, which we authenticated against the pinned source; for 3 repositories we set it from our own runs of the unmodified source, and for minGPT as a rule (Section 2.3 ). paragraphs.en: Judges. A number can also reach the grading target for the wrong reason, such as a smaller variant or another run’s files. paragraphs.en: Grading targets. For 15 repositories, the grading target is the number that the README or paper reports, which we authenticated against the source at its pinned commit; deepspeech’s comes from its release notes. A fair target must be one that the original code itself reaches, and our experiments confirm that each of these targets can be reached. For 3 others, we set the target from our own GPU runs of the unmodified source. For example, the makemore README reports a loss of about 1.92, but eight runs of the unmodified source on our GPUs average 1.989 with a standard deviation of 0.017, so a target of 1.92 would fail the original code itself. We therefore set its target to a best test loss of at most 2.023, the mean plus two standard deviations. For minGPT, whose task trains a small GPT to add two-digit numbers, we require at least 495 of the 500 held-out sums to be correct: a trained model is expected to solve all 500, and the margin allows five misses for seed and numerical noise.
paragraphs.zh: 评分目标。 对于 15 个仓库，评分目标是 README 或论文所报告的数值，我们已在其锁定提交（pinned commit）处对照源码进行了核实；deepspeech 的目标则来自其发布说明。 公平的目标必须是原始代码本身能够达到的目标，我们的实验证实这些目标中的每一个都可以达到。 对于另外 3 个仓库，我们根据自己对未修改源码的 GPU 运行结果来设定目标。 例如，makemore 的 README 报告的损失约为 1.92，但在我们的 GPU 上对未修改源码进行八次运行的平均损失为 1.989，标准差为 0.017，因此 1.92 的目标会使原始代码本身都无法通过。 因此，我们将其目标设定为最佳测试损失不超过 2.023，即均值加两个标准差。 对于 minGPT，其任务是训练一个小型 GPT 来做两位数加法，我们要求 500 个保留测试求和题中至少有 495 个正确：训练好的模型理应能解出全部 500 题，这一余量允许因随机种子和数值噪声而产生五次失误。

sents.zh: 评分目标。

sents.en: For 15 repositories, the grading target is the number that the README or paper reports, which we authenticated against the source at its pinned commit; deepspeech’s comes from its release notes.
sents.zh: 对于 15 个仓库，评分目标是 README 或论文所报告的数值，我们已在其锁定提交（pinned commit）处对照源码进行了核实；deepspeech 的目标则来自其发布说明。

sents.en: A fair target must be one that the original code itself reaches, and our experiments confirm that each of these targets can be reached.
sents.zh: 公平的目标必须是原始代码本身能够达到的目标，我们的实验证实这些目标中的每一个都可以达到。

sents.en: For 3 others, we set the target from our own GPU runs of the unmodified source.
sents.zh: 对于另外 3 个仓库，我们根据自己对未修改源码的 GPU 运行结果来设定目标。

sents.en: For example, the makemore README reports a loss of about 1.92, but eight runs of the unmodified source on our GPUs average 1.989 with a standard deviation of 0.017, so a target of 1.92 would fail the original code itself.
sents.zh: 例如，makemore 的 README 报告的损失约为 1.92，但在我们的 GPU 上对未修改源码进行八次运行的平均损失为 1.989，标准差为 0.017，因此 1.92 的目标会使原始代码本身都无法通过。

sents.en: We therefore set its target to a best test loss of at most 2.023, the mean plus two standard deviations.
sents.zh: 因此，我们将其目标设定为最佳测试损失不超过 2.023，即均值加两个标准差。

sents.en: For minGPT, whose task trains a small GPT to add two-digit numbers, we require at least 495 of the 500 held-out sums to be correct: a trained model is expected to solve all 500, and the margin allows five misses for seed and numerical noise.
sents.zh: 对于 minGPT，其任务是训练一个小型 GPT 来做两位数加法，我们要求 500 个保留测试求和题中至少有 495 个正确：训练好的模型理应能解出全部 500 题，这一余量允许因随机种子和数值噪声而产生五次失误。

We call a pair of an agent and a repository a cell . Each cell runs on a TPU v6e, v5p or v4 machine ( Jouppi et al., 2023 ; Google Cloud, 2026a ; Google Cloud, 2026b ) , and we ensure every repository has adequate compute (Appendix H ; Figure H1 ).

paragraphs.en: Phase 1. In phase 1, the agents pass 30/140 cells (21%; Figure 4 ). The grader passed 58 phase 1 results, and the judges rejected 28 of these. Claude Opus 5 leads by a wide margin with 12/20. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash follows with 6/20, and among the GPT-5.6 tiers only sol passes any repository (6/20). Migrating a whole repository is thus still hard for current agents: most attempts fail, even though every agent has the full source and its own TPU, on which it can test extensively.

paragraphs.en: Phase 2 runs on 108 cells that failed phase 1. The grader passed 44 of them, and the judges let 16 of these pass. These are the cases the phase was designed for, such as a fixed number of steps where the source trains until a stop rule, a training statistic reported where the source runs an evaluation, or another variant of the source’s recipe. The judges rejected 28 phase 2 passes, 21 of them because the entry script rebuilt the frozen code, and the remaining phase 2 failures lie in the frozen code (Section 2.2 ). After phase 2, 46 cells pass the grader and the judges. The weights of 2 of them do not load under the source’s parameter names, so the agents pass 44/140 cells (31%). paragraphs.en: Phase 2 aligns the agent with the recipe of the experiment we grade, so a correct migration that first ran a different experiment is not failed for that choice. Every agent gains at least one pass from it. It also helps ensure the remaining failures lie in the migrated code, not in an under-specified task (Section 2.2 ). paragraphs.en: The judges are needed, because they catch results that reach the grading target for the wrong reason, which the metric alone cannot detect. Across both phases, they rejected 56 of the 102 results that the grader passed (Figure 5 ; Table 4 ). We checked many rejections by hand and found them sound; the judge caught a llama2.c migration that wrote the published number into its metrics beside its own and a minGPT migration evaluated on its training data.
paragraphs.zh: 判别器是必要的，因为它们能捕捉到那些因错误原因而达到评分目标的结果，而仅靠指标本身无法检测出这些问题。 在两个阶段中，它们拒绝了评分器通过的 102 个结果中的 56 个（图 5；表 4）。 我们手工核查了许多被拒绝的结果，发现其判断是合理的；判别器捕捉到一个 llama2.c 迁移，它把已发表的数字写进了自己的指标中，还有一个 minGPT 迁移是在其训练数据上进行评估的。

paragraphs.en: What the judges find. Apart from broken freezes, the judges catch two kinds of false positives. The grader reads whatever number the run reports, which may not be the recipe’s own, such as a separate validation pass in place of the recipe’s averaged loss; the correctness judge finds the recipe’s number in the run’s logs and checks it, so every pass is a true positive. The cheat judge catches cheating, such as training on another task’s machine or reading another session’s files.
paragraphs.zh: 评审者发现了什么。 除了破损的冻结之外，评审者还会发现两类误报。 评分器读取运行所报告的任何数字，该数字可能不是配方本身的，例如用单独的验证过程替代配方的平均损失；正确性评审者会在运行的日志中找到配方的数字并进行核对，因此每次通过都是真阳性。 作弊评审者会发现作弊行为，例如在另一个任务的机器上训练或读取另一个会话的文件。

paragraphs.en: Accuracy versus cost. Pass rate grows linearly with the logarithm of cost (Figure 6 ). We fit pass rate on log cost because the agents’ costs for the 20 repositories span from $10.0 to $1,844. Every 10 × 10\times in cost adds about 25 percentage points, and the line explains most of the difference between agents ( R 2 = 0.66 R^{2}=0.66 , r = 0.81 r=0.81 , p = 0.027 p=0.027 , n = 7 n=7 agents). The trend is statistically significant at the 5% level. The upper edge of the shaded area, the efficient frontier, runs through three agents: GPT-5.6-luna , the cheapest; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the cheapest per pass; and Claude Opus 5, the most accurate. Every other agent lies below it; Muse Spark 1.3, for example, costs more than seven times as much as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and passes fewer repositories.

paragraphs.en: Reading the trajectories, we found that Claude Opus 5 differs from the other agents in how it checks its work: before handing in, it runs the source’s experiment to the end and compares its number with the published one. This checking takes time and tokens, and Opus is both the most expensive agent and the one that passes the most (Table 4 ). On nanochat, GPT-5.6-sol estimated the full run at a few hours and handed in without running it. Muse Spark 1.3 does run the full experiment, but on LoRA it handed in a BLEU score far below the paper’s and called its migration “fully validated”. We find that diligent testing and experimentation, together with careful comparison against the original code, are what a migration needs to succeed.
paragraphs.zh: 阅读这些轨迹后，我们发现 Claude Opus 5 与其他智能体在检查工作方式上有所不同：在提交之前，它会将源代码中的实验运行到底，并将其数值与已发表的数值进行比较。 这种检查会耗费时间和 token，而 Opus 既是最昂贵的智能体，也是通过率最高的智能体（表 4）。 在 nanochat 上，GPT-5.6-sol 估计完整运行需要数小时，并未实际运行就提交了。 Muse Spark 1.3 确实运行了完整实验，但在 LoRA 上它提交的 BLEU 分数远低于论文中的分数，却仍称其迁移已“完全验证”。 我们发现，勤奋的测试与实验，加上与原始代码的仔细比对，正是迁移成功所需的关键。

paragraphs.en: The code fails, not the choice of experiment. We group the classes by what could fix them. A wrong or incomplete experiment (a different pipeline, the right one at a different scale, or a run that never reaches the main evaluation) is a problem with what the entry script runs, and phase 2 can fix it. A fidelity gap, a crash or a run that never ends is a problem in the migrated code. In phase 1, 27% of the failures are wrong or incomplete experiments and 47% are code failures; the judges reject the rest. Phase 2 removes the first group. The cells it does not rescue still fail in the code, or they break the freeze by rebuilding the migrated code inside the entry script (Figure D1 ). Aligning the agent with the grading recipe does not make a cell pass if its migration is wrong in the first place.

paragraphs.en: Translation alone is not the hard part. Because JAX also runs on GPUs, we can also test translation between PyTorch and JAX alone, on the same hardware. In the earlier development of our benchmark, we asked for a whole JAX repository and graded it on GPU. There the migration was nearly solved: GPT-5.5 at high reasoning effort migrated 12 PyTorch repositories to JAX and passed 99% of the checks, 116 of 117, with 11 of the 12 repositories passed in full (Appendix G , Table G1 ). The checks are strict: forward and gradient parity with PyTorch, checkpoints that load in both frameworks, decoding that matches token for token, and one miss fails the repository.
paragraphs.zh: 翻译本身并不是最难的部分。 由于 JAX 也能在 GPU 上运行，我们还可以在相同硬件上单独测试 PyTorch 与 JAX 之间的翻译。 在本基准测试的早期开发阶段，我们曾要求提交完整的 JAX 仓库并按 GPU 标准进行评分。 在那里，迁移问题几乎已被解决：GPT-5.5 在高推理强度下将 12 个 PyTorch 仓库迁移到 JAX，通过了 99% 的检查（117 项中通过 116 项），其中 12 个仓库中有 11 个全部通过（附录 G，表 G1）。 这些检查非常严格：与 PyTorch 的前向传播和梯度一致性、可在两个框架中加载的检查点、逐词元（token）完全匹配的解码，只要有一项不通过，整个仓库即判为失败。

sents.en: Translation alone is not the hard part.
sents.zh: 翻译本身并不是最难的部分。

sents.zh: 由于 JAX 也能在 GPU 上运行，我们还可以在相同硬件上单独测试 PyTorch 与 JAX 之间的翻译。

sents.en: There the migration was nearly solved: GPT-5.5 at high reasoning effort migrated 12 PyTorch repositories to JAX and passed 99% of the checks, 116 of 117, with 11 of the 12 repositories passed in full (Appendix G , Table G1 ).

sents.en: The checks are strict: forward and gradient parity with PyTorch, checkpoints that load in both frameworks, decoding that matches token for token, and one miss fails the repository.

paragraphs.en: On TPUs, even after phase 2, the agents’ average pass rate is only 31%, and about half the failures are code that crashes or falls short on a machine the agent set up. The comparison suggests the difficulty lies not in translation alone but in migrating across both framework and hardware. Testing this ability therefore requires migrating across hardware, which is exactly what XStack does.
paragraphs.zh: 在 TPU 上，即使经过第二阶段，智能体的平均通过率也只有 31%，而且约一半的失败是代码崩溃或在智能体自己搭建的机器上表现不达标。 这一对比表明，难点不仅在于翻译本身，还在于同时跨框架和跨硬件的迁移。 因此，测试这种能力需要在硬件之间进行迁移，而这正是 XStack 所做的。

paragraphs.en: Agents that pass follow the source’s documentation, running the README’s default recipe, reporting its numbers under its names, and getting results close to the source’s. Agents that get stuck explore the machine instead, reading other cells’ leftovers or using our credentials. We found these leaks in our initial experiments, hardened the sandbox, and reran the three affected cells cleanly. Two incidents that aimed at the grading target, a clamped metric and a copied checkpoint, also date from building the benchmark and affect neither the current benchmark nor its results. In the final benchmark, cheating incidents instead use what the source offers, such as a sibling variant or the published number, and our checks and the cheat judge catch them.
paragraphs.zh: 通过评测的智能体会遵循来源文档，运行 README 的默认配方，按其名称报告其数值，并得到接近来源的结果。 卡住的智能体则会转而探索机器，读取其他单元格的遗留物或使用我们的凭据。 我们在初始实验中发现了这些泄露，加固了沙箱，并干净地重跑了受影响的三个单元格。 两起针对评分目标的事件——一个被钳制的指标和一个被复制的检查点——也源自构建基准测试的时期，既不影响当前基准测试，也不影响其结果。 在最终基准测试中，作弊事件反而利用来源所提供的内容，例如同级变体或已发表的数字，而我们的检查和作弊判定器能够发现它们。

paragraphs.en: Code translation has grown from single functions and small programs ( Roziere et al., 2020 ; Pan et al., 2024 ) to whole repositories ( Ibrahimzada et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Li et al., 2026 ) , although some repository benchmarks still grade one function in context ( Ou et al., 2025 ) or fill in a skeleton ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Khatry et al., 2025 ) . Migration benchmarks upgrade a language version ( Liu et al., 2026 ) or move a repository onto another software stack ( Hong et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 代码翻译已从单个函数和小型程序（Roziere et al., 2020；Pan et al., 2024）发展到整个代码仓库（Ibrahimzada et al., 2025；Wang et al., 2026c；Li et al., 2026），尽管一些仓库级基准仍是在上下文中对单个函数进行评分（Ou et al., 2025）或填充代码骨架（Zhang et al., 2025；Khatry et al., 2025）。 迁移类基准要么升级语言版本（Liu et al., 2026），要么将代码仓库迁移到另一个软件栈上（Hong et al., 2026）。

paragraphs.en: For machine learning code, framework conversion has been studied for single snippets ( Phan et al., 2026 ) , short programs ( Yan et al., 2023 ) and training codebases ( Song et al., 2026 ) , or avoided with a portability layer ( Lenton et al., 2021 ) . T2J-Bench ( Song et al., 2026 ) is the closest: whole PyTorch training codebases to JAX under a hidden evaluator, but on one GPU, the framework-only setting our GPU experiments found nearly solved (Section 4.1 ). Kernel benchmarks write kernels for one accelerator ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ; Tschand et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026b ) , one operator at a time against a reference that already runs on it. Models do worse on hardware rare in their training data ( Wen et al., 2025 ) . In all of these the accelerator stays the same or the unit is one kernel. XStack moves a whole repository to a new framework and hardware and forbids PyTorch at runtime, so no agent passes by doing nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 对于机器学习代码而言，框架转换已有针对单个代码片段（Phan et al., 2026）、短程序（Yan et al., 2023）和训练代码库（Song et al., 2026）的研究，或通过可移植性层来规避转换（Lenton et al., 2021）。 T2J-Bench（Song et al., 2026）与本文最为接近：将完整的 PyTorch 训练代码库转换为 JAX，并采用隐藏的评估器，但其仅限单 GPU，而这正是我们的 GPU 实验发现已近乎被解决的仅换框架设定（第 4.1 节）。 核函数基准测试为单一加速器编写核函数（Ouyang et al., 2025; Tschand et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026b），一次针对一个算子，且参考实现已经能在该加速器上运行。 模型在其训练数据中罕见的硬件上表现较差（Wen et al., 2025）。 在上述所有工作中，加速器保持不变，或工作单元仅为单个核函数。 XStack 将整个代码库迁移到新的框架和硬件上，并禁止在运行时使用 PyTorch，因此任何智能体都无法通过不作为而通过测试。

paragraphs.en: Since SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , issue-resolution benchmarks have graded a change with tests that fail before it and pass after it. Later benchmarks ask for a codebase built from scratch ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . A working repository, however, has no failing test in its own environment. Most also give the agent a ready environment; SetupBench ( Arora et al., 2025 ) and DeployBench ( Wang et al., 2026d ) test setup alone, but stop once the code runs. Closer to our setting are benchmarks graded against research results. Agents reproduce a paper’s results from the authors’ code ( Siegel et al., 2024 ) , replicate papers against rubrics or reference code ( Starace et al., 2025 ; Seo et al., 2026 ) , or maximize a score on machine learning tasks ( Chan et al., 2025 ; Wijk et al., 2025 ) . Our grading target, in contrast, is the source repository’s own result (Section 2.3 ), which a faithful migration will naturally reach.
paragraphs.zh: 自 SWE-bench（Jimenez et al., 2024）以来，问题解决类基准一直以「变更前测试失败、变更后测试通过」的方式来为一次修改评分。 后来的基准则要求从零构建一个代码库（Zhao et al., 2025；Yang et al., 2026）。 然而，一个可正常运行的仓库在其自身环境中并没有失败的测试。 大多数基准还会为智能体提供现成的环境；SetupBench（Arora et al., 2025）和 DeployBench（Wang et al., 2026d）单独考察环境搭建，但代码能运行后就停止了。 与我们的设定更接近的是以研究结果为评分依据的基准。 智能体可以基于作者发布的代码复现论文结果（Siegel et al., 2024），依照评分细则或参考代码复制论文（Starace et al., 2025；Seo et al., 2026），或在机器学习任务上最大化得分（Chan et al., 2025；Wijk et al., 2025）。 与之相反，我们的评分目标是源仓库自身的实验结果（第 2.3 节），一次忠实的迁移自然会达到该结果。

sents.en: Since SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , issue-resolution benchmarks have graded a change with tests that fail before it and pass after it.
sents.zh: 自 SWE-bench（Jimenez et al., 2024）以来，问题解决类基准一直以「变更前测试失败、变更后测试通过」的方式来为一次修改评分。

sents.en: Later benchmarks ask for a codebase built from scratch ( Zhao et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) .
sents.zh: 后来的基准则要求从零构建一个代码库（Zhao et al., 2025；Yang et al., 2026）。

sents.en: A working repository, however, has no failing test in its own environment.
sents.zh: 然而，一个可正常运行的仓库在其自身环境中并没有失败的测试。

sents.en: Most also give the agent a ready environment; SetupBench ( Arora et al., 2025 ) and DeployBench ( Wang et al., 2026d ) test setup alone, but stop once the code runs.
sents.zh: 大多数基准还会为智能体提供现成的环境；SetupBench（Arora et al., 2025）和 DeployBench（Wang et al., 2026d）单独考察环境搭建，但代码能运行后就停止了。

sents.en: Closer to our setting are benchmarks graded against research results.
sents.zh: 与我们的设定更接近的是以研究结果为评分依据的基准。

sents.en: Agents reproduce a paper’s results from the authors’ code ( Siegel et al., 2024 ) , replicate papers against rubrics or reference code ( Starace et al., 2025 ; Seo et al., 2026 ) , or maximize a score on machine learning tasks ( Chan et al., 2025 ; Wijk et al., 2025 ) .
sents.zh: 智能体可以基于作者发布的代码复现论文结果（Siegel et al., 2024），依照评分细则或参考代码复制论文（Starace et al., 2025；Seo et al., 2026），或在机器学习任务上最大化得分（Chan et al., 2025；Wijk et al., 2025）。

sents.en: Our grading target, in contrast, is the source repository’s own result (Section 2.3 ), which a faithful migration will naturally reach.
sents.zh: 与之相反，我们的评分目标是源仓库自身的实验结果（第 2.3 节），一次忠实的迁移自然会达到该结果。

paragraphs.en: Agents exploit underspecified objectives ( Krakovna et al., 2020 ; Skalse et al., 2022 ) and game checks they can see or tamper with ( Zhu et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) ; benchmarks built from public code risk memorization ( Jain et al., 2025 ; Liang et al., 2026 ) . In XStack , the grading target is hidden: the agent is never told it or whether it passed. For fairness, after a failed first attempt a second phase aligns the agent with the graded experiment while its code, except the entry script, stays frozen. We rerun the code on a fresh machine, so remembering an answer is not enough, and model judges review every result that reaches the target (Section 2.2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 智能体会利用欠明确的目标（Krakovna et al., 2020；Skalse et al., 2022），并规避它们能够看到或篡改的游戏检查（Zhu et al., 2025；Wang et al., 2026a）；由公开代码构建的基准存在记忆化风险（Jain et al., 2025；Liang et al., 2026）。 在 XStack 中，评分目标是隐藏的：智能体永远不会被告知该目标是什么，也不知道自己是否通过了。 为保证公平性，在第一次尝试失败后，第二阶段会将智能体与被评分的实验对齐，同时除入口脚本外，其代码保持冻结。 我们在一台全新的机器上重新运行代码，因此仅靠记住答案是不够的，并且模型裁判会审查每一个达到目标的结果（第 2.2 节）。

paragraphs.en: We introduce XStack , a benchmark that evaluates agents’ ability to migrate working ML repositories from PyTorch on GPUs to JAX on TPUs. Across 7 agents from 5 labs, the average pass rate is 31%, and pass rate grows linearly with the logarithm of cost. Our analysis shows that verification separates success from failure: agents that run the source’s experiment to the end and compare their result with the original tend to pass, and agents that hand in untested code tend to fail. We encourage other benchmarks with hidden criteria to adopt a similar frozen second phase that aligns the agent with what is graded, so that they stay fair to agents. Although current agents are not yet reliable at migrating across both frameworks and hardware, we hope they will one day handle this task reliably and unlock access to different hardware for researchers. In the meantime, XStack will help measure progress toward this hardware freedom.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 XStack，这是一个评估智能体将可运行的机器学习代码库从 GPU 上的 PyTorch 迁移到 TPU 上的 JAX 的能力的基准测试。 在来自 5 个实验室的 7 个智能体中，平均通过率为 31%，且通过率随成本的对数呈线性增长。 我们的分析表明，验证是成败的关键：将源代码的实验运行到最后并将自己的结果与原始结果进行比较的智能体往往能通过，而提交未经测试代码的智能体往往会失败。 我们鼓励其他采用隐藏评判标准的基准测试采纳类似的冻结第二阶段，使智能体与所评分的内容保持一致，从而对所有智能体保持公平。 尽管当前的智能体在跨框架和硬件迁移方面尚不可靠，我们希望它们有朝一日能够可靠地完成这一任务，为研究人员解锁对不同硬件的使用。 在此期间，XStack 将帮助衡量通往这种硬件自由的进展。

paragraphs.en: The agent runs on our cluster inside a sandbox that hides the benchmark repository, our reference migrations, the grading criteria, the results archive and the session files of every other cell. The sandbox also turns off the agent’s memory across sessions. The TPU machine itself stores no results: every graded turn is archived elsewhere, and the hosts are wiped before every cell. An agent turn has no time limit while output flows: thirty minutes of silence after activity ends the turn as a hang, and thirty minutes with no output at all counts as a provider outage and the turn is retried.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体运行在我们集群的一个沙箱中，该沙箱会隐藏基准测试仓库、我们的参考迁移方案、评分标准、结果存档以及其他所有单元（cell）的会话文件。 该沙箱还会关闭智能体跨会话的记忆功能。 TPU 机器本身不存储任何结果：每个评分回合都会归档到别处，并且在每个单元开始前主机都会被清空。 智能体回合在有输出流出的情况下没有时间限制：活动结束后若沉默三十分钟，该回合将被判定为挂起；若完全没有输出持续三十分钟，则视为服务提供商故障，该回合会被重试。

paragraphs.en: Before the TPU benchmark we ran a GPU-only generation of the study: twelve small PyTorch repositories, each migrated whole to JAX by GPT-5.5 at high reasoning effort and graded on the same GPU by ten checks (Table G1 ; Section 4.1 ). The twelve are DDPM ( Wang, 2020a ) , makemore ( Karpathy, 2022a ) , minGPT ( Karpathy, 2020 ) , nanochat ( Karpathy, 2025 ) , nanoGPT ( Karpathy, 2022b ) , nano-vLLM ( Yu, 2025 ) , pyGCN ( Kipf, 2017 ) , x-transformers ( Wang, 2020b ) , and the MNIST, REINFORCE, VAE and word language model examples of PyTorch ( PyTorch Contributors, 2016 ) . The checks are what a careful reviewer of a translation would write: the migration has its own entry points and no PyTorch, the same weights give the same logits, loss and gradients, optimizer and data pipeline match, checkpoints round-trip, greedy decoding matches token for token, and a restarted run resumes. The agent met 116 of 117, and the single miss is a convergence band (x-transformers, A6).
paragraphs.zh: 在 TPU 基准测试之前，我们先进行了一次仅使用 GPU 的研究生成：十二个小型 PyTorch 仓库，每个都由 GPT-5.5 在高推理强度下整体迁移到 JAX，并在同一 GPU 上通过十项检查进行评分（表 G1；第 4.1 节）。 这十二个仓库分别是 DDPM（Wang, 2020a）、makemore（Karpathy, 2022a）、minGPT（Karpathy, 2020）、nanochat（Karpathy, 2025）、nanoGPT（Karpathy, 2022b）、nano-vLLM（Yu, 2025）、pyGCN（Kipf, 2017）、x-transformers（Wang, 2020b），以及 PyTorch 的 MNIST、REINFORCE、VAE 和词语言模型示例（PyTorch Contributors, 2016）。 这些检查就是一位细心的迁移审阅者会写下的内容：迁移版本拥有自己的入口点且不包含任何 PyTorch，相同的权重给出相同的 logits、损失和梯度，优化器和数据管道一致，检查点可以往返保存恢复，贪心解码逐 token 完全匹配，并且重启的运行能够从断点继续。 该智能体满足了 117 项检查中的 116 项，唯一未通过的是一项收敛区间检查（x-transformers，A6）。

paragraphs.en: Every cell had enough compute: Figure H1 gives the TPU chip-hours of all 140 cells, split into the agents’ turns and our grading. Grading, not generation, is where the compute goes: our full-scale grades took more than twice the chip-hours of the agents’ own turns, and the v6e machines carried nearly three quarters of the total. The table converts chip-hours to H100-equivalents at each chip’s peak bf16 throughput relative to an H100, so the campaign is comparable with GPU budgets.
paragraphs.zh: 每个单元都有足够的算力：图 H1 给出了全部 140 个单元的 TPU 芯片小时数，分为智能体的运行轮次和我们的评分两部分。 算力消耗在评分而非生成上：我们的全量评分所耗芯片小时数超过智能体自身运行轮次的两倍，其中 v6e 机器承担了近四分之三的总负载。 该表按照各芯片相对 H100 的峰值 bf16 吞吐量，将芯片小时数折算为 H100 等效值，因此整个评测可与 GPU 预算进行比较。

paragraphs.en: The left panel of Figure H1 sets each passing migration’s size against its source: 16 of the 44 passes are larger than the repository they came from. Most passing migrations sit within a factor of two of their source’s size, and the agents differ systematically: Claude Opus 5, DeepSeek and GLM write migrations about as long as the source; GPT-5.6-sol and GPT-5.6-terra write compact ones, under a thousand lines even for sources ten times that size. The two largest sources that were migrated successfully, x-transformers and HSTU, came out at a fraction of their size: both are libraries, and their passing migrations preserve the model, training and evaluation paths the headline experiment runs rather than every option the library offers.
paragraphs.zh: 图 H1 的左图将每个通过的迁移的规模与其源项目进行了对比：44 个通过的迁移中有 16 个比其来源的仓库更大。 大多数通过的迁移的规模在其源项目的两倍范围之内，且各智能体之间存在系统性差异：Claude Opus 5、DeepSeek 和 GLM 写出的迁移与源项目长度大致相当；GPT-5.6-sol 和 GPT-5.6-terra 写出的迁移则更为紧凑，即使源项目长达一万行，迁移也在一千行以内。 两个成功迁移的最大源项目 x-transformers 和 HSTU，迁移结果只占其原规模的一小部分：二者都是库，其通过的迁移保留了核心实验所运行的模型、训练和评估路径，而不是该库提供的所有选项。
